title: Keeping family ties
intro: Silat ar-rahim – keeping in touch with our relatives – keeps us connected to Allah and to one another.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, and be good to parents, to relatives, to orphans… <small>(Qur’an, An-Nisa 4:36)</small>

We learned earlier to tell the difference between the close and the wider family, and who belongs to each. Besides being good to our parents, a Muslim has the duty to look after and protect their relatives. Visiting relatives and taking care of them is the best way to keep family ties (silat ar-rahim).

Besides our parents, brothers and sisters, our relatives include our grandfathers and grandmothers, our parents’ brothers and sisters – aunts and uncles on both sides – and their children, our cousins. Keeping family ties is one of the important duties of a believer, commanded in the Qur’an, in the hadith qudsi of Allah (SWT) and in the hadiths of Muhammad (SAW).

learn.title: Hadith qudsi
learn.html: Muhammad (SAW) told us that Allah (SWT) said: “I am the Most Merciful (Ar-Rahman). I created the ties of kinship (ar-rahim) and gave them a name from My own name. Whoever keeps them, I will keep him; whoever cuts them, I will cut him off.” (Tirmidhi)

From this ayah and hadith qudsi we learn that family ties have a very important place in Islam, because whoever keeps family ties keeps a bond with Allah (SWT), and whoever cuts them cuts their bond with Him. So it is important to stress:

items: keeping family ties is like keeping our bond with Allah, which brings good in this world and the next
cutting family ties is like cutting our bond with Allah, which takes away many of life’s values

learn.html: Keeping family ties matters because of the love between relatives, which grows in childhood. That is why it is important to visit relatives with our parents while we are children, and to get to know their children. For relatives’ children to love each other, and for that love to last, we should:

items.label: Spend as much time together as we can
Stay as guests with each other in the holidays
Help each other with school and maktab work

learn.text: The benefits of keeping family ties

items: the reward for following the Sunnah
easier everyday life in the dunya

learn.html: We should keep family ties even with relatives who don’t visit us back. If we do that, it shows we are doing it only for the sake of Allah (SWT), and we expect our reward from Him.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “Keeping family ties is not returning a visit. Keeping family ties is visiting the one who does not visit you.” (Bukhari)
Cutting family ties has serious consequences in this world, and especially on the Day of Judgement, as the Prophet (SAW) warned.

learn.title: 🏙️ In our community
learn.html: Many of our families in Erie have relatives in Bosnia and around the world. A phone or video call, a message or a visit in the summer holidays is also a way of keeping family ties.

practice.title: Who are my relatives?
practice.prompt: Tap everyone who belongs to our relatives (rahim), then tap Check.

options.why: A classmate can be a good friend, but is not a relative.
We treat everyone kindly, but the shopkeeper is not family.

practice.title: Match it up
pairs: Allah keeps His bond with you
Allah cuts His bond with you
Visiting the one who doesn’t visit you

questions.q: What is the best way to keep family ties?
options: Waiting for them to come first

questions.q: Which name of Allah did He give to the ties of kinship (rahim)?
What happens to the one who keeps family ties?
options: Allah keeps His bond with him

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) say true keeping of family ties is?
options: Visiting the one who doesn’t visit you

questions.q: When does love between relatives grow?
When are the consequences of cutting family ties especially hard?

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 Who, besides our parents, belongs to our relatives? What results come from keeping family ties, and what from cutting them?
🌟 What are the benefits of keeping family ties? What is keeping family ties according to the hadith of Muhammad (SAW)?
😊 Talk with your muallim: remember some of the best moments you spent with your relatives. Describe them and try to explain why that feeling was so good.
📞 Choose a task (1): Talk with your parents about relatives your family rarely or never visits – and agree to visit or call them.
👴 Choose a task (2): Talk with your grandfather and grandmother about what families used to be like. How often did they visit each other, and how big were the families then?
📋 Choose a task (3): Make a table of your close and wider family: name, how they are related to you, and how close you are (✓ we know each other, ✓✓ we visit often, ✓✓✓ we visit very often).
